primitives.name: Player Spacing Clustering
primitives.verbatim_quote: For each lineup, run **k-means on time instants**, where the "objects" are milliseconds and similarity is the vector of pairwise player-dyad distances.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'t': 'time instant in milliseconds', 'd_{ij}(t)': 'distance between players i and j at time t in cm', 'X(t)': 'vector of all pairwise dyad distances at time t'}
primitives.assumptions: 1. Dyad distances capture positional structure; 2. Time instants are independent; 3. Clustering identifies stable tactical configurations.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When player movement becomes stochastic or exceeds 5-minute lineup duration threshold.

layer2.mapping: Clustering kernel maps temporal sequences of dyad vectors to discrete game phases using k-means.
layer2.telemetry: Cluster assignment per millisecond; transition matrix of cluster switches.

primitives.name: Multidimensional Scaling
primitives.verbatim_quote: Characterize clusters with profile plots (average dyad distances per cluster) and 2-D **multidimensional scaling (MDS)** of average between-player distances to visualize spacing patterns.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'D_{ij}': 'mean pairwise distance between players i and j in cluster c', 'Y_c': '2D embedding of cluster c via MDS'}
primitives.assumptions: 1. Average inter-player distances preserve topological structure; 2. MDS preserves relative distances in low-dimensional space.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When inter-cluster variance dominates intra-cluster variance, reducing discriminability.

layer2.mapping: MDS provides geometric representation of player spacing that mirrors tactical configurations.
layer2.telemetry: 2D visualization of cluster configurations; Euclidean distance between embeddings.

primitives.name: Phase Labeling by Position
primitives.verbatim_quote: Label each moment offense/defense/transition by the mean x-position of the five players (transition when average x in [-4, +4] around half court); assign each cluster to the phase it mostly contains.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'x_{avg}(t)': 'average x-coordinate of five players at time t', 'P(t)': 'game phase label {offense, defense, transition}'}
primitives.assumptions: 1. Mean x-position correlates with offensive/defensive orientation; 2. Transition occurs near center court.
primitives.breakdown_regime: During fast breaks or unconventional spacing where x-position fails to reflect actual phase.

layer2.mapping: Position-based labeling maps continuous spatial coordinates to discrete tactical labels.
layer2.telemetry: Per-millisecond phase classification; proportion of cluster belonging to each phase.

The core methodology employs k-means clustering on time-series player dyad distances to segment gameplay into distinct tactical phases. Each time instant is represented by a vector of pairwise distances between players on court. These vectors are clustered into six groups, consistent across lineups, indicating stable tactical configurations. Multidimensional scaling (MDS) then projects these clusters into a 2D space to visualize positional patterns. Phase labels (offense/defense/transition) are assigned based on average x-position of players, enabling linkage between spatial arrangement and shooting outcomes. The transition matrix captures dynamic switching behavior between clusters, suggesting temporal dependencies. However, the method assumes that dyad distances fully encapsulate positioning, and that simple x-position proxies accurately classify phases—both assumptions may fail under complex or fast-paced scenarios. The lack of statistical tests on shooting performance limits causal inference. This framework supports GSI’s probabilistic modeling through cluster-based FG% estimation and GSE’s tactical reasoning via phase transitions.
